imageDescript: the treeline/brush patch across the corner from where live
personText: Seeing the deciduous trees and brush change with the seasons, seeing the trees swaying in the wind during storms, seeing the snow laying on the coniferous trees in winter, all help us not feel so penned in by our ever-expanding neighborhood.  Hearing all the bird activity there is amazing.  We received notice that they are building another apartment complex behind there, and we are worried about losing this small patch of nature
dogText: He loves to explore/sniff the edges of the brush, and in some winters we'll make a foot path through the snow and weave back through the edge of the trees. He loves exploring and smelling things there.
walkText: Ample sidewalks which allow us to stay off the roads (some of which get very busy and with drivers not being mindful of their speeds).  With the sightlines, we can see other dogwalkers and either change direction, cross the street, or find ways to make sure each dog can safely navigate

imageDescript: little sprigs growing out of a tree root stretching near the sidewalk
personText: It's fun to notice the little details like this, something I wouldn't see unless I was out with my dog and he hadn't stopped to check it out.
dogText: He loves stopping to sniff and explore things as we go.
walkText: He seems to enjoy the stimulation of checking out various things that cross our path.

personText: Last year I happened to cross to a side of the street I don't usually walk on at the end of the cherry season, and realized this glorious cherry tree was near the sidewalk.  I've been watching the tree all year, and noticed yesterday the cherries were turning red.  So exciting!
dogText: If it's not ground level or moving (like a squirrel or large bird), he doesn't seem to notice.  Although he does tend to appreciate the shade from taller trees during warm days!
walkText: Many choices to vary our walk depending on what activity is going on around us, we often change course or simply just cross the street to avoid loud noises (garbage/construction trucks, construction noise such as roofing), as my dog is sensitive to those things.  We just adjust our route and keep going to avoid coming too close to those kinds of things (or to avoid close contact with other dog walkers), and he seems to enjoy the cognitive stimulation of changes rather than the same route every day

imageDescript: someone has set a bowl of water out for passing dogs
personText: I usually try to bring water on our walks on warm days, but if I forget there are a few places that we've passed on our walks where someone has set out bowl of water.  It's very thoughtful!
dogText: Somedays he just notices and passes by the water bowl, other days he is grateful for a little drink along the way.
walkText: There are a few places like this with either water bowls or an enclosed box with dog treats that are quite sweet to see around the neighborhood.  It feel welcoming as we pass through various streets on our wanderings.

imageDescript: part of a beautifully crafted yard that I enjoy walking by.
personText: There are so many creative spaces in our neighborhood, and while i don't feel creative, I really love seeing what people have done with their spaces.  This yard in particular is filled with lots of gorgeous and unusual plant choices, and sprinkled in here and there are little things like this plastic lizard. It's fun to see the whimsy in the lush garden they've created.
dogText: He doesn't seem to notice as much, at least not yet.
walkText: it's just lovely to see different things as you walk

imageDescript: fallen tree branch after the storms on wednesday
personText: I hadn't really noticed the downed branch, but Charlie thought it was interesting so we made a stop.
dogText: He seemed to delight in whatever smells where on the branches.  He was very curious!
walkText: Always something new to see, and in my dog's case, smell.

personText: The wildflower fields surrounding the sport fields are just so lush and abundant, I love seeing the changes as the seasons progress .  Always so much birdsong through there, it's fun to pull out the Merlin app and see who all is singing.
dogText: He loves walking through the park, that way we are far away from any loud trucks or other loud noises.  He seems to understand it's a safe stretch, especially on garbage pickup days when he can hear the truck sounds echoing all through the neighborhood.  He does seem to act a little freer when we are on this path rather than on sidewalks walking past houses.
walkText: It's a quiet space to just breathe.  Seeing our residential Redtail now and then early in the morning, hanging out in a tree or on the backstop, seeing the moon reflect on undisturbed snow in the winter, it's just so wonderful to have quite space to connect with the earth.  Good for my mental health, anyway.

imageDescript: The retention pond near the interstate
personText: Lots of birdlife to see and hear, it's peaceful even with the roar of the highway, and it's another space where we can leave the sidewalk if we choose.
dogText: Lots of good smells from the ducks and geese and turkeys, Charlie loves to leave the sidewalk and explore.  He also knows we are getting close to home.
walkText: To be able to see green spaces, even if small, is so important for mental health.  To breathe in the air, see the changes in the landscape through the year, to feel the wind, see the changes in the sky, it's very grounding.

imageDescript: brush/tree line coming back around to where we started
personText: I love being closer to the treeline and being able to see into the little patch of woods, all the detail hidden beneath the canopy.
dogText: He loves the smells, gets excited by the movement of critters scurrying back for cover., and he knows we are almost home which always makes him happy.
walkText: This path is usually safe in all seasons, people aren't spraying the grass in this stretch, it's usually not salted in the winter (which is always a struggle, finding places to walk that aren't dangerous to my dog's feet).
